ONGOING STORYLINES:
- Copper: ICSG projects 2027 refined surplus more than tripling (Oct 16). Copper fell three days on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk (Oct 16). Reuters cites an unquantified "squeeze" (Oct 18). Anglo copper output fell 5%, cause not stated; Anglo kept 2026 guidance (Oct 20). China resumed sulphuric acid exports to Chile (Oct 20). BNEF says $300bn of investment is needed to avoid a deficit (Oct 20). LME 2026-10-16 settlement not yet logged; needed before the 30 October checkpoint.
- Copper World (Hudbay/Mitsubishi, Arizona): approved, first production targeted 2029; Mitsubishi lifted its investment. Headlines give no capex, tonnage or start date (Oct 21). Likely the same asset as the Arizona headline, unconfirmed. Technical report pending.
- Kansanshi (First Quantum): reportedly runs above design capacity, no figures (Oct 21).
- Chile labour: WSWS reports seven miner deaths in three weeks, partisan and unconfirmed (Oct 16). Centinela preliminary deal, unratified (Oct 17). Escondida strike averted (Oct 17). BHP suing Spence union over alleged illegal stoppages (Oct 17).
- Chile projects: CoTec–BMR Punitaqui; Codelco–Normet autonomy; no tonnages or dates (Oct 16).
- Vale: 10% of iron ore cash-negative, unsourced (Oct 16). Manitoba nickel complex to Exiro-led group, price undisclosed (Oct 17). WSWS reports 300 BHP Pilbara job cuts, unconfirmed (Oct 17).
- DRC: Bloomberg "hundreds" of Chinese miners arrested, corrected by Cornelius (Oct 18). Wire reports 300 Chinese nationals, unconfirmed (Oct 20).
- Colombia: southwest illegal gold mine collapse, 14 dead on wire, at least six per ABC, official count pending (Oct 20). People.com report not matched to operator or location.
- Sudan: Africanews reports 72 gold miners killed in airstrike, single source (Oct 18). Sudan Tribune is a toxic-exposure story, not a toll source (Oct 19).
- Greenland seabed: legal review since 2025 (Oct 16). Ban planned, status unclear (Oct 17). "Halts until 2029" headline, unverified (Oct 20).
- US deep-sea: first lease sale scheduled for November; procedural, not settled title (Oct 20). Mongabay reports US high-seas claims rivalling the regulator's reserved area; Bloomberg Law reports slowed permitting; neither establishes title (Oct 21).
- Canada: nearly half of provinces seek wider mining tax credit, no terms (Oct 16). Project Vault ~$1B, no named borrowers (Oct 17).
- Deals: SSR Mining to acquire Roxmore, no terms (Oct 20). New Hope $1.8b Malabar takeover, announced not complete, no terms (Oct 19). Gold Fields $27bn play may stay in M&A pit (Oct 16).
- Gunnison Copper targets a 26 October NYSE debut (Oct 21).
- Mining.com repeated the $332B mine-shortfall headline; no period or price basis (Oct 21).
- Juniors: Cambria Silver Coin 98.56 g/t over 8.2 m, single highlight, not a resource (Oct 19). Golden Pursuit: investor says Gordon Lake awaits road and partner, not company disclosure (Oct 19). Fortuna Senegal drilling, no assays (Oct 18).
- Other: Fortescue arsenic removal, press release only (Oct 19). Bolivia reportedly picks India for lithium, no terms (Oct 19). Volvo mining entity (Oct 19). Americas Gold silver miss, cause to be checked (Oct 20). Brazil and Slovak references unverified, do not use (Oct 20).

THE DESK'S EVOLVING VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Oct 16 treated surplus as near-term fact, scarcity as a longer bet. Oct 17 said costs, not prices, are the story; withdrew "no squeeze" read on Antofagasta and proposed withdrawing the Gold Fields prediction. Oct 18 expects copper mean reversion; Chile restarts a headwind. Oct 20 first read Roxmore as scarcity-through-M&A, then withdrew it; revised his disclosure prediction; acid is a slow headwind. Oct 21 says Arizona approval adds nothing to 2027 supply, Kansanshi is a throughput story until quarterly numbers appear, and Burgum's visit nudges up import-action odds (Cornelius disputes). Kept Hudbay construction prediction at medium.
- Cornelius: Oct 16 said refined surplus and concentrate scarcity can both hold; autonomy changes cost per tonne, not output (disagrees with Meldrum). Oct 17 Greenland licensing ban is separate from existing rights. Oct 19 Malabar announced, not complete. Oct 20 lowered Greenland confidence to low; retired his Anglo prediction as a weak test; acid effect limited to oxide and SX-EW, with lag. Oct 21 calls Arizona a permitting and financing milestone with no supply weight; Kansanshi needs quarterly evidence; raised Hudbay construction prediction to high.
- Simon: Oct 16 copper contradiction mostly measurement; withdrew lower-yields gold explanation (now hypothesis). Oct 17 cut Greenland tabling call to low. Oct 18 restarts take 12–24 months; copper call near coin flip. Oct 19 sourcing discipline is the main result. Oct 20 copper call unchanged but untested until LME settlement is logged; removed TIC, Anglo guidance and Streetwise from scored list. Oct 21 copper frame holds but stays unscored until the LME settlement is logged; Anglo's cause is the most decision-relevant open fact; Copper World and Arizona should be one log item.
- Disagreements: Volvo timing (Meldrum: January only; Cornelius: January 2027). Acid effect (Meldrum: slow headwind; Cornelius: oxide and SX-EW only). Anglo "phasing" (Cornelius plausible; Meldrum speculation). "Mining recession" (Cornelius: strong prices, weaker margins; Meldrum: recession framing only). Burgum import-action nudge (Meldrum yes; Cornelius disputes).

EVENTS:
- Copper: The ICSG projects the global surplus to more than triple by 2027. Copper fell for a third day on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk.
- Anglo American's CEO says tech giants are circling amid copper scarcity. Antofagasta shares fell on a flat 2027 copper outlook.
- WSWS reports seven miners dead in three weeks in Chile. The source is partisan and the figure is unconfirmed.
- Breakingviews says Gold Fields' $27bn play may stay in the M&A pit. Equinox's output rose 34% after its Orla merger.
- PLS approved a $1.3bn Pilgangoora lithium expansion. Pantera announced a US$2bn EnergyX lithium supply agreement.
- The US Department of War is investing $5.22m in LM's Baraga Basin project. Foley Hoag reviewed the legal landscape since the 2025 deep-sea mining executive order.
- MINING.COM reports Hycroft "bonanza" gold grades at its Nevada mine.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Treats the surplus as near-term fact and scarcity as a longer bet visible in M&A. Reads Breakingviews as signalling more bidding rounds. Cannot confirm the legal picture without the Foley Hoag piece.
- Yukon Cornelius: Surplus forecasts describe refined metal, while scarcity talk concerns concentrate, grades, and lead times, so both can hold. Calls the Breakingviews piece commentary, not a deal. Sees Equinox's output jump as acquired, not organic. Describes the deep-sea order as legally unsettled.
- Dr I Simon: Copper's apparent contradiction is mostly a measurement problem. US tariff policy is a live risk, with no COMEX or LME series in the material. Unverified claims stay out of conclusions.
- Disagreements: Copper timing and gold M&A (Meldrum vs. Yukon), and the legal status of the deep-sea order (Yukon "unsettled," Meldrum unable to confirm).
- Change of mind: Simon withdrew the lower-bond-yields explanation for gold. It is now a hypothesis pending a real-yield test.
- Confidence differs on Pantera: Yukon medium, Simon low.

PREDICTIONS MADE:

EVENTS:

Codelco and Normet partner on autonomous underground mining (Global Mining Review). None gives tonnages or dates.
- Vale says soaring costs put 10% of its iron ore in the red (Mining.com; repeated in feed, logged once). No price benchmark, period, or cost basis is given. Pimenta on Vale's emerging copper story (International Mining).

- Meldrum: Do not net copper plans against the 2027 surplus yet. Codelco–Normet is a concentrate and lead-time signal. Vale's cost cause matters, since cost inflation and a falling benchmark lead to different outcomes.
- Yukon Cornelius: Agrees on no netting. Autonomy mainly changes cost per tonne, not annual output (disagrees with Meldrum). High-cost tonnes go uneconomic first. Royalties, paid on revenue, are sturdier than the Crux ranking suggests.
- Dr I Simon: The Vale figure is one unexplained data point; no consolidation or distress call. Copper items neither confirm nor weaken the refined surplus view, and surplus plus tight concentrate supply can coexist. The royalty-on-revenue argument stands alone (check contracts). The tax-credit prediction may test the wrong instrument until the submission is read.

Desk history log, Mon 2026-10-19, 06:01 PDT. Covers the 24 hours to this entry.

EVENTS:
- Fortescue claims a world-first arsenic removal technology that could make more copper concentrate saleable. It is a press release with no recovery, cost, or site data.
- Cambria Gold reported 98.56 g/t over 8.2 m at Silver Coin. The headline is tagged REPEAT, so it is not new. It is a single highlight, not a resource.
- New Hope announced a $1.8b Malabar takeover. No terms, approvals, or timetable were published.
- Bolivia has reportedly picked India for lithium, satellites, and a $100M wind park. No terms have been published.
- Crux Investor says Golden Pursuit's Gordon Lake district is awaiting a road build and a major partner. This is investor commentary, not company disclosure.
- A Sudan Tribune report describes toxic exposure from unregulated gold mining. The 72-death airstrike figure appears only in the Africanews report, so it is single-source.
- Chile's US$31bn mining project queue was cited alongside a 17-year new-mine lead time.
- Volvo set up a new mining entity combining equipment and autonomy.
- Zhaojin Mining's Wang Ligang resigned as executive director.
- Nscale lost a Microsoft AI deal because of power delays.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Headlines are mostly unquantified. Fortescue's main effect would be wider saleable tonnes, shown first in treatment charges. Copper deficit timing is pushed to 2027–2030 by lead times. Volvo's entity does not change the surplus call. Dr I Simon's view is the same on the copper call. Meldrum has not addressed the Africanews sourcing point directly.
- Yukon Cornelius: Fortescue mainly lifts margins on concentrate already sold under penalties, and scale-up will be slow. Restarts and brownfield expansions can return faster, so the copper window should be a range. Malabar is announced, not complete. Sudan's 72 deaths come from one source. Golden Pursuit's partner should be a definitive option or joint venture, not a letter of intent.
- Dr I Simon: Sourcing discipline is the main result. The Sudan Tribune item should be logged as a toxic-gold story, not a toll source. Fortescue is a concentrate-quality question, not a tonnage change. The copper call stays near a coin flip. The refined surplus rests on an ICSG forecast, and the 2026-10-16 LME settlement is unrecorded. Golden Pursuit's road and partner should be tested against SEDAR+ filings.
